full_judgment: 4. Defendant Nos. 1 and 2 contested the suit by the filing joint written statement denying the plaint case contending, inter alia, that admittedly, Umed Ali was the original owner of the suit khatian, who died leaving behind 3(three) sons named Abdul Majid, Abdul Karim and Abdur Rahman and 2 (two) daughters named Sayeda Banu and Hashmater Nessa. Each of the sons inherited 4 annas share in the land of the suit khatian. But Hashmater Nessa and Sayeda Banu did not physically possess any land in the suit khatian. After the death of Sayeda Banu, her share in the suit khatian devolved upon her only son, Jabol Haque, defendant No. 3, who transferred the suit properly along with other land to defendant Nos. 1-2 for a valuable consideration of Taka 2000 by the deed duly executed on 28-12-1983 and registered on 23-4-1984. Defendant No. 1 was the son of Abdul Karim and defendant No. 2 was the son of Abdur Rahman. During the life time of Sayeda Banu, the lands of the suit khatian were possessed equally by 3 (three) sons of Umed Ali named Abdul Majid, Abdul Karim and Abdur Rahman. Prior to the purchase of the suit property, defendant Nos. 1 and 2 were in possession thereof. They have been possessing the suit land since their purchase. The suit was false and was liable to be dismissed with cost.
